key.text:
How rotation works, as drawn

Each login has one rule:
● in rotation  new workers start on the one with the most room
○ standby  used only when every login in rotation is at its limit
◌ off  never used

space on view 6 cycles a login's rule. It saves at once, with u to undo, so there is no confirm step.

Rules are per computer, not per repo: every repo here shares them. /desk-setup asks for them once. desk-q view 6 changes them after.

The same rules apply to Codex logins.

The emails and plans are example data (Ben's logins). Nothing in desk names them.

setup.text:
If you pick "Choose which rotate", a second question lists the logins to tick. Every login you leave unticked goes on standby. AskUserQuestion shows 4 options at most, so with more than 4 logins setup lists them in the reply and asks you to name the ones to rotate.

Codex gets the same question, after Claude, when more than one Codex login is signed in.

states.text:
With one login and no rotation set, home keeps today's line: "Claude usage  5h … · 7d …".

Standby and off logins are read less often than logins in rotation: a probe costs tokens on that login, and none of its workers write readings. Their cells show "as of" when the reading is over 5 minutes old.
